title: The Pardon
subtitle: Coffee, pastries, family, memories of simpler times, and an ominous chain.

trails.title: Heartfelt Blessing
trails.description: How would you calculate the distance between two reuniting parties?

content.text:
Marianne,​​

I hope you'll understand why I couldn't say goodbye properly, as I understood when you did the same. By the time I finally learned where you had gone, you were already deep underground, facing poisonous gases. Anyway, I just want this letter to reach you safely.

The "XII" required a medic, and although I sensed there was something distinct about this squad, I accepted; it would keep me on the front lines longer, and Mr. Creius's invitation could not have been more timely. Of course, this means I had to leave immediately with the squad. We're moving to the Eastern Front soon, where some of my comrades are reportedly stationed. 

While I'm now part of the "XII," I've been granted permission to operate independently in the eastern region for a while. I'm hoping to locate some of my former comrades from my order to see if any might be interested in joining the Foundation.

Marianne, I know your family has an unusual constitution, and you might think overly cautious, but I have to say this: after prolonged combat in poisonous gas conditions, you really should get a full medical examination.

Wishing you all the best.

Marsha

items.text: The Pardon
After yet another night passes, the hidden chapel once again welcomes the light of day.
Time passes, reaching near to midday, and the grassy courtyard holds its quiet with a patience born of humility.
The awaited figure finally appears at the forest's edge. She's spent the night tending to her wounds.

items.speaker: Female Gargoyle
items.text: My, Marie, thou hast returned!
She holds back the urge to embrace her family—her arms are filled with a silver tray of coffee and pastries.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Coffee?

items.speaker: Female Gargoyle
items.text: Yes, just to thy liking—no milk, no sugar. There are also vanilla macarons and Mont Blanc besides.
The bright colors of the pastries feel all the more surreal for the darkness she has gone through.
Sentinel takes the warm coffee from her aunt's hands and takes a small sip in disbelief. Of course, it's far from the quality of a Parisian café, but at this moment, it is more than enough.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Where did you get these desserts?
The woman clasps her hands together, wearing a faint, bittersweet smile.

items.speaker: Female Gargoyle
items.text: Look, who is here, my sweetie.
Sentinel takes notice of the tall figure stepping into view—a face she has not seen for a long time.

items.speaker: Immanuel
items.text: Marianne.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Father.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: What brought you here?

items.speaker: Immanuel
items.text: A pardon hath been issued by the president. Thou art free.

items.speaker: Immanuel
items.text: As for Ladislas, he is gravely ill. His stubbornness was ever bound to lead to trouble.
He ends the topic with mild discontent.

items.speaker: Immanuel
items.text: Hmph. To answer thy question: I am here to gather ye. We are to depart.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: So, you are now the leader of the clan?

items.speaker: Immanuel
items.text: Verily. After all we have suffered under this war, someone must lead the Ténébrun family's reconstruction. I seek to re-establish contact with those of our kin with whom we have lost fellowship.

items.speaker: Immanuel
items.text: The hand of Manus Vindictae has not yet fallen upon Paris. I have purchased a number of dwellings in Montmartre. They are to be our temporary homes until the conflict between the Manus and the Foundation reaches its end.
The Ténébrun patriarch makes an imperturbable gesture as he turns to face Agnès.

items.speaker: Immanuel
items.text: Agnès shall be sent to our cemetery in Rouen.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Cemetery?
She cannot—or will not—accept the words.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: But Agnès is not dead; she's simply ... Ladislas said there was a reason behind her—
Marianne raises her eyes and meets her father's mournful gaze.

items.speaker: Immanuel
items.text: This is what comes of disrespecting tradition, Marianne. Thou wert too easily swayed by Ladislas's maddened words.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: He lied to us?

items.speaker: Immanuel
items.text: Nay. I believe not that such was his intent. He was simply too fervent in his pursuit of Gnosis.

items.speaker: Immanuel
items.text: There is no record in the family archives that suggests any sort of prophecy should befall our kin in so strange a form.

items.speaker: Immanuel
items.text: Agnès's condition is the result of a tragic accident, nothing more. There is no divine meaning behind it whatsoever.

items.speaker: Immanuel
items.text: Her fear of the war was too great. She simply faltered in the casting of her arcane skill and petrified her body to the core.

items.speaker: Immanuel
items.text: That is all.

items.speaker: Immanuel
items.text: I know well that Agnès meant a great deal to both Ladislas and thee, but she was only an ordinary child. She was not an angel descended from heaven.

items.speaker: Immanuel
items.text: Though it doth bring sorrow for me to say, we must all come to accept that no miracle shall ever come to Agnès—she will forever remain a statue.
He reaches out to take his daughter's shoulder, already bearing too many burdens.
Their conversation falls away into a pensive silence before the "statue" of Agnès.
He is the first to leave, attending to more pressing matters—several moving trucks are already parked outside the church.
Trembling chains pierce the air.

items.speaker: Ladislas
items.text: Marianne, thou hast returned. How ...?
He staggers forward, as if pushed by some invisible force, drawing closer to Sentinel.
In his palm lies a chain that glints coldly in the sunlight.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: S**t, I thought Father was only ... Have you truly fallen ill?

items.speaker: Ladislas
items.text: That I have. But what of thee, Marianne? Art thou not in a condition far graver than my own? Or art thou simply too blind to see it?
He babbles on. With every word, his madness grows. There seems to be no trace of his old humility left.

items.speaker: Ladislas
items.text: Thy soul is stained with the wickedness of sin! Thou art as miserable as I ... O Lord, I-I can smell the stench of hell upon thee ...

items.speaker: Ladislas
items.text: Thou hast passed through the gates of hell and returned, Marianne ... How wretched ...

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: You are ill, Ladislas. Gravely so.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Take a moment's rest in the quiet of a sanatorium upon reaching Paris, won't you? It ought to do you good.
Ladislas squints like a child sharing a secret.

items.speaker: Ladislas
items.text: Perhaps I shall. But thou wilt not return with us, wilt thou?

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: I am yet undecided. Perhaps I will ...

items.speaker: Ladislas
items.text: Nay. Nay. Thou must not! Thou must never return!

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Why?

items.speaker: Ladislas
items.text: I see that which others cannot, and I see it in thee. Thou art not who thou once wast! Inside thee, there is ...

items.speaker: Ladislas
items.text: A demon, the demon which doth linger in our veins. It hath opened its eyes, its wretched eyes!

items.speaker: Ladislas
items.text: Aaagghh!
Ladislas howls in pain, his body shaking violently. The chain in his hand clatters and rings.

items.speaker: Ladislas
items.text: Thou cannot return—cannot turn back! For there is no path left for thee ...

items.speaker: Ladislas
items.text: But ... but I desire naught more than to aid thee, my dear cousin. Yea, I shall help us all, but most especially thee—to atone for my transgressions ...
The shaking stops, and all at once, he bows with a gesture of utter submission, presenting the chain before her.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Ladislas?

items.speaker: Ladislas
items.text: These shackles are a soul-binding chain—a cage, yea, but I beg thee accept them.

items.speaker: Ladislas
items.text: And I shall devote my life to prayer over thee—both night and day—that thy soul shall not be shaded in eternal darkness.

items.speaker: Ladislas
items.text: May thy blood be washed clean one day. May it nourish the soil when thou art laid to rest. May thy journey to hell yet be graced by God's mercy.
Another not-so-light burden to serve as a constant reminder of the limits of evil.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: And if I refuse these shackles?

items.speaker: Ladislas
items.text: It mattereth not. I shall pray for thee still, as I have ever done.
A sudden impulse moves her to look at the statue of Agnès.
At last, she takes the chain.
The metal hangs in her hand; its weight feels far greater than its size would merit.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Tell my father that I will not return.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Until the true conflict is brought to an end.
